## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Khandhakapucchāvāra* (also known as the *Khandhakapucchā*) is the sixth treatise of the *Parivāra*, the final collection of the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral; Horner 1966]. The text comprises a catechism that poses questions on the contents and legal issues of each chapter of the Khandhakas, surveying the ten chapters of the *Mahāvagga* and the twelve of the *Cullavagga* [SuttaCentral; Horner 1966]. While framed around queries regarding the number of offences occurring across these chapters, I.B. Horner observes, following the commentary, that it inquires into the categories and classes of offences rather than raw numerical counts [Horner 1966]. The text begins with a question and answer regarding ordination (*upasampadā*) with its provenance and demonstration, determining the relevant offences according to eminent sentences [Horner 1966].

No canonical parallels are cataloged on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. Automatically computed text reuse identified by DharmaNexus shows extensive sharing within the Pali tradition, particularly with the *Saṅgāyana-pucchā vissajjanā Vinayapiṭaka* (303 matches), the *Parivāra-aṭṭhakathā* (29 matches), and Vinaya sub-commentaries including the *Pācityādiyojanā* and *Vimativinodanī-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects minor algorithmic alignments with Sanskrit and Tibetan Vinaya and terminological materials, such as the Sanskrit *Mahāvyutpatti* and the Tibetan translation of the *Vinayasūtra* (D4117) [DharmaNexus]. Complete English translations have been published by I.B. Horner and Bhikkhu Brahmali [Horner 1966; SuttaCentral].
